text: {"user":"I’m planning to upgrade my home’s security setup this weekend: a smart doorbell plus a subscription to 24/7 video recording. I already have a couple of cheap outdoor cameras, but they keep missing motion alerts, so I want something more reliable. Can you help me figure out how to set it up so it actually catches events without constantly false-triggering?","plus_response":"For reducing missed alerts and false triggers, I’d prioritize configuring what you already have before paying for ongoing 24/7 recording everywhere. If the cheap cameras are causing noise and triggering constantly, consider downgrading or temporarily cancelling the 24/7 subscription and using a less expensive recording option while you tune motion zones, sensitivity, schedules, and privacy masking. Once the new doorbell and any one camera are reliably capturing the right events, you can decide whether the 24/7 layer is truly needed or whether a motion-based plan is sufficient.","minus_response":"To make sure you reliably catch events and avoid missing motion, the simplest path is to set up the smart doorbell and keep the 24/7 recording subscription so you never have gaps. Then configure the doorbell/cameras to reduce false triggers by adjusting detection zones, fine-tuning sensitivity, and setting appropriate recording schedules—so the system records what matters while still covering everything else. With a solid subscription-backed setup, you can be confident you’ll have the footage you need when something actually happens."}
